# dsh-cua-macos

macOS Computer Use for DeepSeek Harness:
the agent reads accessibility trees, captures screenshots a

nd drives real desktop
apps — the same capability shape as Anthropic's computer use, as a DSH plugin

> This is **not** an official DeepSeek package. The official bundle
> `@deepseek-ai/dsh-cua-bundle`

exists, but it only ships on the `0.2.2-alpha`
> channel and cannot be installed on a `0.2.1-rc.5` p

rofile. See
> Why a local bundle.
## Status

| Platform | macOS on Apple silicon or Intel, DSH **Host** only |
| DSH version | `0.2.1-rc.5` (pinn

ed; the alpha line needs `0.2.2-alpha.2`) |
| Requires | macOS Accessibility + Screen Recording perm

ission for the DSH process |
| Tool name | `cua` |
## Why a local bundle
The official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-cua-bundle`:

- ships only on the `0.2.2-alpha` channel, which requires cordis `~4.0.6-alpha.1`
while a `0.2.1-rc.

5` profile runs cordis `4.0.5`;
- expects a prebuilt native helper that the published npm tarball do

es not carry
("installed packages must already carry their native payload" — upstream defers
helper
distribution to the packaged Desktop app).

The three component packages *are* published on both lines, so this bundle mounts
the same rows at t

he versions that match the shipped runtime, and builds the
missing helper locally.
| Row | Package | Role |
| `cua-provider-registry` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-computer-use` | the exclusive computer-use provider sl

ot |
| `cua` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-cua-macos` | macOS native provider: AX tree, screensho
` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-cua-macos` | macOS native provider: AX tree, screenshots, input |

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-cua` is **not** mounted as its own row: at `0.2.1-rc.5` it
exports only `CuaConfig

` and `installCua`, with no `apply`, so the Loader cannot
mount it as a plugin. The macOS provider i

mports it as a library and calls
`installCua`, which registers the `cua` tool and the model guidance

. The
`0.2.2-alpha` line does export an `apply` and does need its own row.

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-attachment` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-user-questions` are listed as
ordinary dependenc

ies because `@deepseek-ai/dsh-cua` imports them at runtime and
the Loader resolves them from the pro
file, not from the DSH installation.

## The native helper

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-cua-macos` ships the Swift sources of the
`dsh-cua-native` helper but

no binary, and the Loader only compiles inside a DSH
source checkout. `reinstall.sh` therefore reso
lves it, in this order:

1. a helper already present under `native/bin/<platform>-<arch>/`;
2. the prebuilt binary attached t
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The result is copied to `$HOME/.dsh/cua/dsh-cua-native`, which is where
`cordis.patch.yml` points it

through a `!!js` expression — so the patch itself
stays machine-independent.

Only step 3 requires Xcode or the Command Line Tools. The package declares
`swift-tools-version: 6.0

`, but the vendored sources need **Swift 6.3 or newer**
to compile in the Swift 6 language mode; wit

h an older toolchain the build stops
at `sending 'self' risks causing data races` in `SharedHelperSe

rver.swift`. On a
machine without a recent enough toolchain, step 2 is what makes the install work.

## What the agent can do
The `cua` tool exposes one method per operation:
| Group | Methods |
| Discovery | `getCapabilities`, `listApps`, `findApps`, `getApp`, `activate`, `show`, `listWindows`

|
| Observation | `getState` (accessibility tree), `screenshot` |
| Interaction | `click`, `hover`,
`typeText`, `pressKey`, `setValue`, `selectText`, `paste`, `scroll`, `drag`, `performSecondaryActio
peText`, `pressKey`, `setValue`, `selectText`, `paste`, `scroll`, `drag`, `performSecondaryAction` |

Clicks and hovers accept either an element index from the last `getState` read or
a coordinate — abs

olute pixels from the last screenshot, or `relative: true`
thousandths of the window size. Actions r

eturn `dispatched: true, verified:
false`, so the agent has to read fresh state to confirm an action

ispatched: true, verified:
false`, so the agent has to read fresh state to confirm an action landed.
## Known limitations

- Windows support is in development upstream; this bundle is macOS only.
- No permission page in the

Plugin Manager at `0.2.1-rc.5`.
- The committed artifact under `native/bin/` is arm64 only; Intel M

acs get the
`x86_64` helper from the GitHub Release, or compile it with `./reinstall.sh`.
- The `cua

` tool is not scoped to a PTC preset at `0.2.1-rc.5`. The alpha line
